title: Camel Emoji 🐪 Meaning: Hump Day, Deserts and the Magi
description: 🐪 is the one-humped camel: hump day Wednesdays, desert trips, the Three Kings at Epiphany, and the eye of the needle. See its meanings and how it differs from 🐫.
summary: The 🐪 camel emoji shows a dromedary, the one-humped Arabian camel. People use it for Wednesday as "hump day," for desert travel and the Middle East and North Africa, for the Magi's journey at Epiphany, and occasionally as a crude slang reference to tight clothing.
meaning: The most common joke is about Wednesday. Hump day is the middle of the work week, the hump you climb over before the weekend, and a 2013 insurance commercial with a camel shouting "hump day!" through an office made the link permanent. "Happy hump day 🐪" still circulates every Wednesday in group chats and office Slack channels.

Literally, 🐪 marks deserts, caravans, and travel in places where dromedaries live, such as Morocco, Egypt, Jordan, and the Arabian Peninsula. Tourists post it with camel rides near the pyramids or in the Sahara. It also symbolizes endurance, since camels can go long periods without drinking, and people use it after a grueling day: "survived it like a camel 🐪."

In Christian contexts the camel is associated with the Magi. The Gospel of Matthew does not say how the wise men traveled, but art and tradition picture them arriving on camels, so 🐪 appears around Epiphany on January 6, Three Kings Day in Spain and Latin America. Jesus' saying that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God also makes 🐪 a shorthand in sermons and Bible studies.

There is also a crude slang meaning: "camel toe" describes the outline visible through very tight pants or leggings. 🐪 sometimes appears in jokes about it, so be aware of that reading in teasing comments about clothing or gym outfits. Outside of that specific setting, almost nobody will read the emoji that way, and most uses are about Wednesdays, deserts, or the Magi.

contexts.label: On Wednesdays
contexts.body: "Happy hump day 🐪" is a midweek ritual in offices, school group chats, and radio show posts. It means the week is half over. It is light and workplace-friendly, though some people use "hump day" with a suggestive wink, so the setting matters.

contexts.label: At Epiphany
contexts.body: Parishes and families post 🐪 with 👑 and ⭐ for the visit of the Magi, celebrated on January 6 or on the nearest Sunday in many countries. In Spain and Latin America, Three Kings Day parades and gifts make it a major celebration, and children's posts often show camels carrying the kings.

contexts.label: When traveling
contexts.body: Desert treks, camel rides, and trips to Morocco, Egypt, Dubai, or Jordan get 🐪 in captions, frequently with 🏜️ and ☀️. It can also simply signal heat or thirst: a sweltering summer day becomes "camel weather," and a friend who never drinks water during a long hike gets called a camel.

confusedWith.difference: 🐫 is the Bactrian camel with two humps, native to Central Asia. 🐪 is the dromedary with one hump, the camel of Arabia and North Africa. In practice people use them interchangeably for hump day.
🦙 is a South American relative of the camel, with no hump and a long woolly neck. It is used for llamas, alpacas, and quirky humor, not deserts or hump day.

avoid: Do not use 🐪 as a stand-in for Arab or Middle Eastern people; that reduces real cultures to a stereotype.
Avoid it in comments on someone's outfit, where it may be read as the crude slang meaning.
design: A tan or sandy brown camel in side view with a single hump, long curved neck, and knobby legs. Most designs show it standing or mid-stride. Its two-humped counterpart, 🐫, is drawn in the same style, and the number of humps is the only reliable difference.

faqs.q: Why is the camel the hump day emoji?
faqs.a: Wednesday is called hump day because it is the middle of the work week. A widely seen 2013 TV ad featuring a talking camel celebrating hump day tied the animal to Wednesday, and 🐪 has been the go-to emoji since.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🐪 and 🐫?
faqs.a: 🐪 is the dromedary camel with one hump, found in Arabia and North Africa. 🐫 is the Bactrian camel with two humps, from Central Asia. People use either one for hump day and deserts.

faqs.q: Did the Three Kings ride camels?
faqs.a: The Gospel of Matthew does not say. Tradition and art pictured them on camels, likely because they came from the East, and some read Isaiah 60:6, which mentions camels bringing gold and frankincense, as foreshadowing the scene.

faqs.q: Is the camel emoji ever rude?
faqs.a: Usually not, but it can be. "Camel toe" is crude slang for a visible outline through tight pants, and 🐪 sometimes stands in for it. On its own, though, it almost always means hump day or deserts.
